Fix \(\rho\in I\), the realized dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\), and \(C=C_n(\rho)\) with positive reference cell probability.  For each \(s\in S\), the sharp-null completion assigns the observed value to both treatment labels of every observed unit.  Thus, for every \((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s})\in\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), all values entering the candidate arm counts, means, and variances are known.  When the displayed nondegeneracy conditions fail, the stipulated value \(X'_{n,s}=c_s-1\) is also known.  Therefore \(X'_{n,s}\) and \(C'_n(\rho)\) are imputable for every candidate first-stage action.  The identical argument makes every candidate rank \(U'_{nksi}\), contrast \(R'_{kj}\), and totalized degenerate value imputable.  If \(C_s=1\), a quota-respecting \(z'_{n2s}\) then determines \(R'_{2j}\) and \(T'_j\); if \(C_s=0\), chronology generates no stage--\(2\) coordinate.

By definition, \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\) imposes exactly the following conditions: for every \(s\in S\), the holdout has size \(\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor\), the stage--\(1\) assignment has quota \(m_{n1s}\), and the recomputed full signed label is \(C'_n(\rho)=C\); in addition, for every \(s\) with \(C_s=1\), the generated stage--\(2\) assignment has quota \(m_{n2s}\).  The preceding paragraph proves imputability on every such history.

Conversely, any quota-respecting chronological history has first-stage coordinate in \(\prod_{s\in S}\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\).  If its recomputed label is \(C\), it passes the sole cell restriction.  Chronology then supplies, and supplies only, one quota-respecting stage--\(2\) vector for every \(s\) with \(C_s=1\).  Hence the history belongs to \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\).  Positivity of \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\) makes normalization legitimate.  Since \(S\) is finite, all products and enumerations above are finite; no two-coordinate argument or additional conditioning event has been used.

For \(t\in S\), let \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) be the holdout and stage--\(1\) assignment history in stratum \(t\).  The holdout and stage--\(1\) design assumptions make \((\mathcal H_{nt})_{t\in S}\) mutually independent.  The selector \(X_{n,t}\) and its sign event are stratum-local measurable functions of \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) and the fixed potential outcomes.  Conditional on all first-stage histories, the stage--\(2\) assumption gives mutually independent stratum-local kernels.  Equivalently, those kernels may be pregenerated and revealed only in recruited strata.  Hence, for \(j=(C,s)\), measurable \(B_0\), and \(p_{nt}=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{X_{n,t}>c_t\}\), finite-product independence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,E_{n,C}(\rho)\}\\
&\quad=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,X_{n,s}>c_s\}
\prod_{t\in S\setminus\{s\}}p_{nt}^{C_t}(1-p_{nt})^{1-C_t}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The same identity with \(B_0\) equal to the whole space gives the cell probability.  Whenever that probability is positive, division cancels every signed factor indexed by \(t\ne s\).

Under \(\mathsf R_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}^{0,\mathrm{base}}\), the first-stage candidate mass is a finite product over \(t\in S\), and the completion and maps \(X'_{n,t}\) are stratum-local.  Thus its signed cell probability is \(\prod_{t\in S}(p'_{nt})^{C_t}(1-p'_{nt})^{1-C_t}\).  Restriction to \(C'_n=C\) divides by this product, and the subsequently generated stage--\(2\) reference law is again a product over \(\{t:C_t=1\}\).  Positivity of \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\) licenses this division.  The same finite-product argument applies to the independent stage--\(1\) blocks and independent stage--\(2\) coordinates in the Gaussian experiment.

For the active coordinate, write
\[
X_s=a_j(\rho)h_s+Z,
\qquad
T_j=d_j(\theta_j)h_s+r_j(\rho,\theta_j)Z+v_j(\rho,\theta_j)E,
\]
with independent standard normal \(Z,E\).  At zero drift, conditioning on \(X_s>c_s\) is conditioning on \(Z>c_s\), so integrating over \(E\) gives the defining equation for \(q_{\alpha,j}\).  Under the local alternative, the condition becomes \(Z>c_s-a_j(\rho)h_s\); integrating over \(E\), then normalizing by this event's probability, gives exactly \(\Pi_j\).  All inactive-stratum positive and negative inequalities were retained until their factors canceled, and the argument used only finiteness of \(S\).

Fix a block and abbreviate its size by \(N\).  Since \(\max_i x_i^4\le\sum_i x_i^4\), the fourth-moment assumption implies
\[
\max_i(B_i-\bar B)^2
\le\left\{\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^4\right\}^{1/2}
\le\sqrt{M_4N}.
\]
The variance margin gives \(\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^2=(N-1)S_B^2\ge(N-1)\epsilon\).  Division proves the first displayed bound in the statement.  For normalized midranks, \(0\le U_i^0\le1\), so \(\max_i(U_i^0-\bar U^0)^2\le1\); the same variance-margin division proves the second bound.  Positive limiting shares imply \(N_{nks}\to\infty\) for every \((k,s)\), and, because \(K\times S\) is a fixed finite set, the convergence is uniform over all blocks.  Positivity of \(\epsilon\) justifies every division.

The definition of \(\kappa_j\) and Cauchy--Schwarz give \(\lvert\kappa_j\rvert\le1\).  Since \(\rho\in[\rho_0,1-\rho_0]\) and \(0\le\cos^2\theta_j\le1\),
\[
v_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2
=1-\kappa_j^2(1-\rho)\cos^2\theta_j
\ge1-(1-\rho)=\rho\ge\rho_0>0.
\]
This calculation is pointwise for every member of the finite active set \(J\), so the same bound is uniform over \(j\), \(\rho\), and \(\theta\).  It concerns only the limiting Gaussian covariance and makes no finite-\(n\) covariance assertion.

Fix one admissible baseline array \(B=(B_n)_n\); no supremum over different arrays is taken.  We establish the two approximations for arbitrary sequences \(\rho_n\in I\), \(h_n\in H\), and \(\theta_n\in[0,\pi/2]^J\).  Compactness then turns the sequential conclusion into the asserted uniform one: otherwise a violating sequence would have a convergent subsequence, to which the same calculations apply.  Finiteness of \(S\), \(K\), and \(J\) permits simultaneous control of every coordinate.

For a stage--\(1\) block, abbreviate \(N=N_{n1s}\), \(m=m_{n1s}\), \(\delta=h_s/\sqrt n\), and let \(G\) be the random complement.  Conditional on the balanced assignment, each complement arm count is hypergeometric.  The hypergeometric mean and variance formulas, \(m/N\to1/2\), and \(\rho\in I\) give, uniformly along every such sequence,
\[
\frac{g^1}{N}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{2},
\qquad
\frac{g^0}{N}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{2}
\quad\text{in probability}.
\]
For \(f_i\) equal to \(B_i-\bar B\), \((B_i-\bar B)^2\), or \((B_i-\bar B)(U_i^0-\bar U^0)\), the variance identity for simple random sampling without replacement, Cauchy--Schwarz, and the bounded fourth moment imply
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{i\in G}f_i-\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i=o_{\mathsf P}(1).
\]
The same holds after intersection with either treatment arm because the preceding count limits bound both random denominators away from zero with probability tending to one.  Thus the exceptional selector-totalization event vanishes, both arm variances converge to the full finite-population variance, and linearizing the random denominators around \((1-\rho)N/2\) yields
\[
X_{n,s}=A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s+X^0_{n,s}+o_{\mathsf P}(1),
\]
where \(X^0_{n,s}\) is the variance-standardized complement contrast of the fixed \(B\)-values.  The additive effect contributes exactly \(\delta\) to the unstudentized treated-minus-control contrast, while within-arm centering removes it from both sample variances.

For the rank expansion, let \(K_N(\delta)\) be the ordered-pair crossing count.  Complete-randomization inclusion probabilities give
\[
\mathsf E(\text{treated crossed-pair count})
=\frac{m(N-m)}{N(N-1)}K_N(\delta).
\]
Expanding its variance over pairs of directed crossing edges, overlapping pairs contribute at most a constant times \(NK_N(\delta)\), while disjoint pairs have covariance of order \(N^{-1}\) and contribute at most a constant times \(K_N(\delta)^2/N\).  Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\text{treated crossed-pair count})
\le C\{NK_N(\delta)+K_N(\delta)^2/N\}.
\]
The uniform pair-spacing premise gives \(K_N(\delta)=O(N^{3/2})\).  Since the null rank-sum standard deviation is of order \(N^{3/2}\), the centered crossing term is \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\) after studentization, while its expectation converges to \(b_{1j}h_s\).  If \(d_i\) is the number of ranks crossed by unit \(i\), then \(\sum_i d_i\le2K_N(\delta)\), \(\max_i d_i\le N\), and
\[
\frac1N\sum_i\left(\frac{d_i}{N}\right)^2
\le\frac{2K_N(\delta)}{N^2}=O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Hence the observed normalized ranks have the same limiting variance and covariance as the baseline midranks.  The pair-spacing limit also forces the squared empirical tie masses to vanish, so their variance tends to \(1/12\).  Therefore
\[
R_{1j}=b_{1j}h_s+R^0_{1j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1).
\]
The same calculation in stage \(2\), conditionally on recruitment and using its independent complete randomization, gives \(R_{2j}=b_{2j}h_s+R^0_{2j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1)\).

Conditional on a holdout outside an event of vanishing probability, random-denominator linearization expresses \((X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})\) as a fixed-dimensional vector of complete-randomization contrasts plus \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\).  The maximum-influence bounds in \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\) hold for every scalar projection, so \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\mbox{-}population\mbox{-}vector\mbox{-}clt}\) applies by Cram\'er--Wold.  With balanced signs \(W_i=2Z_i-1\), the identity \(\mathsf E(W_iW_l)=-1/(N-1)\) for \(i\ne l\) gives by direct covariance expansion
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})longrightarrow
\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}.
\]
The complement indicator contributes \(1-\rho\) to the covariance and its square root to the selector standard deviation.  The history-conditional stage--\(2\) randomization is independent.  Thus the joint limit is
\[
\mathcal N\!\left(
\begin{pmatrix}A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\\ b_{1j}h_s\\ b_{2j}h_s\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}
1&\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&0\\
\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&1&0\\
0&0&1
\end{pmatrix}
\right).
\]
The residual-scale lemma keeps every projected limit nonsingular.

Condition on a realized dataset for the Fisher reference.  Its fixed completed stage--\(1\) value is \(B_i+\delta Z_i\).  Boundedness of \(h\), the fourth-moment condition, and \(\delta=O(n^{-1/2})\) make its empirical first four centered moments differ from those of \(B\) by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\).  The crossing-degree bound above makes the squared empirical difference between its normalized ranks and the baseline midranks \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\).  Candidate labels are newly completely randomized, so every candidate contrast is null-centered; candidate holdouts are newly sampled, and candidate stage--\(2\) assignments are independently generated after the candidate cell is known.  Applying the same finite-population vector theorem conditionally on the realized completed array shows, in \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\)-probability, convergence of the pre-cell reference vector to the preceding Gaussian vector with every drift equal to zero.

Because the Gaussian limits have continuous cdfs, convergence over rectangles implies uniform cdf convergence.  Fixed thresholds then give convergence of every joint numerator and signed cell denominator.  The sampling-selection margin bounds the sampling denominators below by \(\epsilon\) eventually, and the reference-selection margin does so with probability tending to one.  The finite-product factorization and \(\mathrm{lem{:}conditioning\mbox{-}ratio\mbox{-}transfer}\) therefore give the asserted conditional sampling and reference cdf limits for every sequence of parameters, hence uniformly over the compact parameter domain.

For critical values, \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\) implies that every limiting conditional score has a continuous positive density.  Gaussian tail bounds and compactness of the finite primitive family, \(I\), the angle cube, and the fixed thresholds place all null critical values in one compact interval.  On a slightly larger interval, continuity and positivity give a common density lower bound.  The quantile clause of the conditioning-ratio lemma therefore transfers \(q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}\) uniformly.

Let \(a_n=d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\).  The preceding argument gives \(a_n\to0\).  Let \(Z_n(\rho,h)\) be the reference distance.  For every \(m\), choose \(N_m\) so large that, for \(n\ge N_m\), \(a_n\le1/m\) and \(\sup_{\rho,h}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{Z_n(\rho,h)>1/m\}\le1/m\).  Taking \(N_m\) increasing and setting \(\eta_n(B)=1/m\) on \([N_m,N_{m+1})\), with finitely many initial values enlarged, produces one deterministic decreasing sequence with both asserted properties.

Finally, on the selected event, split according as the random critical value is within \(\zeta\) of \(q_{\alpha,j}\).  On this good event the rejection probability is bracketed by the sampling cdf at \(q_{\alpha,j}\pm\zeta\); the bad event has conditional probability tending to zero because the sampling cell probability is at least \(\epsilon\).  Gaussian anti-concentration makes the bracket width vanish as \(\zeta\downarrow0\).  The factorization lemma identifies the limit as \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\).  This proves the common per-array transfer, including random complement counts, both studentizers, rank stability, the imputed zero-null reference, and moving quantiles.

Let \(\gamma_2\) be standard Gaussian measure on \(\mathbb R^2\), and define
\[
\mathcal O(c,z)=[c,\infty)\times[z,\infty),
\qquad
\mathcal T(c,z)=Q^{-1}\{Q(c)Q(z)\}.
\]
Minkowski interpolation of two such orthants is the orthant having the interpolated thresholds.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}ehrhard\mbox{-}borell\mbox{-}convex\mbox{-}equality}\), and using \(Q^{-1}(u)=-\Phi^{-1}(u)\), yields
\[
\mathcal T((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)z_0+tz_1)
\le(1-t)\mathcal T(c_0,z_0)+t\mathcal T(c_1,z_1).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal T\) is jointly convex.  If \(Z\) is standard normal, then \(Q(Z)\) is uniform on \((0,1)\), and for \(y>c\),
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal T(c,Z)>y\}=\frac{Q(y)}{Q(c)}.
\]
Therefore \(\mathcal T(c,Z)\) has the distribution of a standard normal conditional on exceeding \(c\).

Put \(v=\sqrt{1-r^2}>0\), \(W(c,z,e)=r\mathcal T(c,z)+ve\), and
\[
\mathcal A(c,q)=\{(z,e):W(c,z,e)\le q\}.
\]
For \(r\ge0\), \(W\) is convex, and hence
\[
(1-t)\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)+t\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)
\subseteq
\mathcal A((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)q_0+tq_1).
\]
Take \(q_i=q_\beta(r,c_i)\).  The two sets on the left each have Gaussian measure \(1-\beta\).  Ehrhard--Borell and the inclusion imply that the set on the right has measure at least \(1-\beta\).  Since the independent term \(vE\) supplies a positive continuous density, the quantile is unique, and
\[
q_\beta(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)
\le(1-t)q_\beta(r,c_0)+tq_\beta(r,c_1).
\]
This proves convexity.

If \(r=0\), this quantile is the constant \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\beta)\); if \(c_0=c_1\), chord equality is immediate.  Conversely, suppose \(r>0\), \(c_0\ne c_1\), and chord equality holds.  Equality must then hold in the preceding Gaussian-measure comparison.  The equality clause of the cited lemma says that \(\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)\) and \(\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)\) are parallel half-spaces or equal modulo Gaussian null sets.  They are not half-spaces: their boundaries are the nonaffine graphs
\[
e=\{q-r\mathcal T(c,z)\}/v,
\]
because \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to c\) as \(z\to-\infty\) and \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to\infty\) as \(z\to\infty\).  Equality modulo null sets of these closed convex sets implies equality, so the two boundary graphs would make \(\mathcal T(c_0,z)-\mathcal T(c_1,z)\) constant.  Its limit at \(-\infty\) is \(c_0-c_1\).  If this constant were nonzero, the elementary Mills inequalities
\[
\frac{\phi(x)}{x+x^{-1}}<Q(x)<\frac{\phi(x)}x\qquad(x>0)
\]
would make \(Q(\mathcal T(c_0,z))/Q(\mathcal T(c_1,z))\) tend to zero or infinity as \(z\to\infty\), whereas its defining identity makes that ratio equal to \(Q(c_0)/Q(c_1)\).  Hence the constant is zero, which forces \(c_0=c_1\), a contradiction.  These are exactly the asserted equality strata.

Fix \(j=(C,s)\), \(\rho\), and \(\theta_j\), and abbreviate \(a=a_j(\rho)>0\), \(d=d_j(\theta_j)>0\), \(r=r_j(\rho,\theta_j)\), and \(q_\alpha=q_\alpha(r,c_s)\).  For \(u\in(\alpha,1)\), the selected upper-quantile definition gives
\[
\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\ge u
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B_u(h_s):=dh_s+q_u(r,c_s-ah_s)-q_\alpha\ge0.
\]
The selected-quantile theorem makes \(B_u\) continuous and convex.  Because \(u>\alpha\), \(B_u(0)=q_u(r,c_s)-q_\alpha(r,c_s)<0\).  As \(h_s\to\infty\), the threshold tends to \(-\infty\), the selected quantile tends to the ordinary finite Gaussian upper-\(u\) quantile, and \(dh_s\to\infty\).  Hence \(B_u(h_s)\to\infty\).  A continuous convex function that is negative at zero and tends to infinity has a unique positive crossing and is nonnegative thereafter: at any crossing \(x>0\), all right secant slopes are at least \((B_u(x)-B_u(0))/x>0\).  Thus the power superlevel set above \(u\) is an upper interval.

Compactness of \(H\) makes \(\ell_s=\min_{h\in H}h_s\) attainable, and positivity gives \(\ell_s>0\).  Since all other represented coordinates satisfy \(h_s\ge\ell_s\), the upper-interval property proves
\[
\min_{h\in H}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\ge u
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge u.
\]
This is coordinatewise and therefore needs no product structure for \(H\) and no restriction on the finite cardinality of \(S\).  Finally, \(\theta_j=\pi/2\) gives \(r=0\) and power
\[
Q\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_{2j}h_s\}>\alpha
\]
for every \(h_s>0\).  Thus every optimized cell value and the global optimized value are above \(\alpha\).  Their above-size superlevel predicates are identical under \(H\) and the coordinate vector \(\ell\), so both the value and the complete argmax correspondence are unchanged.

Fix an active pair and suppress its index.  Put \(t=\sqrt{1-\rho}\), \(a=At\), \(\gamma=\kappa t\), \(d=b_1\cos\theta+b_2\sin\theta\), \(r=\gamma\cos\theta\), and \(v=\sqrt{1-r^2}\).  For \(h=\ell_s>0\), define
\[
L=c-ah,\quad K=q_\alpha(r,c)-dh,\quad
u_0=\frac{c-rq_\alpha(r,c)}v,\quad
u_h=\frac{L-rK}v,\quad
D_h=\frac{\phi(K)Q(u_h)}{Q(L)}>0.
\]
Let \(\mu(x)=\phi(x)/Q(x)\).  Differentiation of the Gaussian upper-tail ratio and of the null critical equation, justified by \(v^2\ge\rho_0\), gives
\[
q_r=\frac{\mu(u_0)}v,
\qquad P_d=hD_h,
\qquad P_r=\frac{D_h}{v}\{\mu(u_h)-\mu(u_0)\}.
\]
The normal hazard satisfies \(\mu'(x)=\mu(x)\{\mu(x)-x\}\).  Integration by parts for a standard normal conditioned below by \(x\) gives \(\mu'(x)=1-\operatorname{Var}(Z\mid Z>x)\); positivity of this nondegenerate variance and the elementary Mills inequality \(\mu(x)>x\) give \(0<\mu'(x)<1\).  Define
\[
\bar s=\frac{\mu(u_0)-\mu(u_h)}{u_0-u_h}
\quad\text{if }u_0\ne u_h,
\qquad
\bar s=\mu'(u_0)\quad\text{otherwise}.
\]
The mean-value theorem gives \(0<\bar s<1\), and direct subtraction gives \(u_0-u_h=h(a-rd)/v\).  With \(d'=b_2\cos\theta-b_1\sin\theta\) and \(r'=-\gamma\sin\theta\), the chain rule yields
\[
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}
=d'+\frac{\gamma\sin\theta\,(a-rd)\bar s}{v^2}.
\]
The identity \(\cos\theta\,d=b_1+\sin\theta\,d'\), together with \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1\), gives
\[
a-rd=t\Delta-\gamma\sin\theta\,d',
\qquad
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}
=\mathcal Ld'+\frac{\kappa t^2\sin\theta\,\Delta\bar s}{v^2},
\]
where
\[
\mathcal L=1-\frac{\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s}{v^2}>0,
\]
because \(v^2-\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s\ge1-\gamma^2\ge\rho>0\).

Now \(d'>0\) on \([0,\theta_0)\), \(d'(\theta_0)=0\), and \(d'<0\) on \((\theta_0,\pi/2]\), where \(\theta_0=\arctan(b_2/b_1)\).  If \(\Delta>0\), the derivative above is strictly positive throughout \([0,\theta_0]\), so no maximizer lies there.  If \(\Delta<0\), it is strictly negative throughout \([\theta_0,\pi/2]\), while \(P_\theta(0)=hb_2D_h>0\), so every maximizer lies in \((0,\theta_0)\).  If \(\Delta=0\), its sign is exactly that of \(d'\), proving that \(\theta_0\) is the unique maximizer.  Compactness of the angle interval supplies existence.  The calculation is cellwise, so it applies simultaneously to every member of any finite \(J\).

Fix a jointly realizable active stage--\(1\) block and center its baseline values.  Write \(\sigma^2\) for their limiting variance and \(\lambda\) for the pair-spacing slope.  Convolve the empirical law \(N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{B_i}\) with the uniform density on an interval of width \(\delta_N=u_\star/\sqrt N\), where \([0,u_\star]\) is contained in the pair-spacing window, and denote the resulting density by \(f_N\).  The ordered-pair convention, including half weights at ties and endpoints, gives
\[
\|f_N\|_2^2
=\frac{2}{N^2\delta_N^2}\int_0^{\delta_N}K_N(u)\,du
=\frac{2}{u_\star^2}\int_0^{u_\star}N^{-3/2}K_N(x/\sqrt N)\,dx
\longrightarrow\lambda.
\]
The variance of \(f_N\) is \(\sigma_N^2+\delta_N^2/12\), and the definitions of \(A\) and the positive limiting share imply \(\sigma_N^2\to\sigma^2>0\).

For any centered density \(f\) with variance \(\sigma_f^2>0\), set \(a=\sqrt5\,\sigma_f\) and \(g(x)=3(1-x^2/a^2)_+/(4a)\).  Since \((1-x^2/a^2)_+\ge1-x^2/a^2\),
\[
\int fg\ge\frac{3}{4a}\left(1-\frac{\sigma_f^2}{a^2}\right)=\frac{3}{5a},
\qquad
\int g^2=\frac{3}{5a}.
\]
The inequality \(\int(f-g)^2\ge0\) therefore implies \(\|f\|_2^2\sigma_f\ge3/(5\sqrt5)\).  Applying this to \(f_N\) and passing to the preceding limits gives \(\lambda\sigma\ge3/(5\sqrt5)\).

The pair-spacing condition removes asymptotic atoms, so the normalized midrank has limiting variance \(1/12\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)\le\sigma/\sqrt{12}\).  Joint realizability supplies, for the same array,
\[
A=\frac{\sqrt{r_1}}{2\sigma},
\qquad b_1=\sqrt3\lambda\sqrt{r_1},
\qquad \kappa=\frac{\sqrt{12}\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)}\sigma.
\]
Consequently
\[
\frac{A\kappa}{b_1}
=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)}{\sigma^2\lambda}
\le\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}\sigma\lambda}
\le\frac{5\sqrt{15}}{18}.
\]
All denominators are positive by the variance, pair-spacing, and share premises.  The proof is blockwise and hence uniform over the finite active set.

Fix \(j=(C,s)\) with \(\Delta_j\ge0\), and write \(P(\rho,\theta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\theta,\ell_s)\).  In the notation of the weight-side proof, differentiation of the tail ratio gives
\[
P_a=h\mu(L)\left[Q\!\left(\frac{q-dh-rL}{v}\right)-P\right]<0
\quad(r>0),
\qquad
\operatorname{sign}(P_r)=\operatorname{sign}(rd-a).
\]
The strict inequality holds because, for \(r>0\), the rejection probability conditional on \(Z=z\) is strictly increasing in \(z\), so its value at the truncation boundary is below its selected-tail average.  Every individually maximizing angle obeys \(\theta\ge\theta_0\) by the weight-side theorem.  On this interval, \(\cos\theta\,d\le b_1\), whence
\[
a-rd=t\{A-\kappa\cos\theta\,d\}\ge t\Delta\ge0.
\]
Thus \(P_r\le0\).  Since \(a_\rho=-A/(2t)\) and \(r_\rho=-\kappa\cos\theta/(2t)\),
\[
P_\rho=-\frac{AP_a+\kappa\cos\theta\,P_r}{2t}>0
\]
at every maximizing \(\theta<\pi/2\).  At \(\theta=\pi/2\), the power is the constant pure-stage--\(2\) value \(p_2=Q\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_2\ell_s\}\).

At the largest holdout, \(t^2=\rho_0\).  The inward angular derivative from \(\pi/2\) is
\[
\phi\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_2h\}
\left[b_1h-\kappa t\{\mu(c)-\mu(c-Ath)\}\right].
\]
Since \(0<\mu'<1\), the bracket is greater than \(h(b_1-\kappa At^2)\).  The realizability lemma and \(\rho_0<1/2\) give
\[
\frac{\kappa At^2}{b_1}
\le\rho_0\frac{5\sqrt{15}}{18}<1,
\]
so pure stage \(2\) is strictly improvable there.

Let \(M_j(\rho)=\max_\theta P(\rho,\theta)\).  If \(M_j(\rho)=p_2\), the endpoint strict improvement gives \(M_j(\rho)<M_j(1-\rho_0)\).  Otherwise a maximizing nonpure angle lies at or above \(\theta_0\), and its fixed-angle power increases strictly all the way to the endpoint; maximizing again there preserves the strict inequality.  Hence
\[
M_j(\rho)<M_j(1-\rho_0)\qquad(\rho<1-\rho_0).
\]
Because \(J\) is finite, choose a cell binding in \(F(1-\rho_0)=\min_jM_j(1-\rho_0)\).  Its preceding strict inequality implies \(F(\rho)<F(1-\rho_0)\), proving uniqueness of the maximizing holdout.  At the endpoint, a binding cell uses an individual maximizing angle.  The weight-side theorem and the strict inward derivative place it in \([\theta_{0j},\pi/2)\), with equality precisely when \(\Delta_j=0\).  Every slack cell may use exactly its full \(V^\star\)-superlevel set, as stated.

Before scaling, the stage--\(1\) density equals \(16/5\) on \([-1/10,1/10]\) and \(1/5\) on the remainder of \([-1,1]\).  Direct piecewise integration gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(B)=\frac{203}{1500},
\qquad
\int f^2=\frac{53}{25},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\{B,F(B)\}=\frac14\mathsf E|B-B'|=\frac{1393}{15000}.
\]
Scaling by \(L=53\sqrt3/80\) multiplies variance by \(L^2\), divides the pair slope by \(L\), and multiplies the covariance by \(L\).  The stage--\(2\) uniform law has variance \(625/1849\) and pair slope \(43/(50\sqrt3)\).  Since every block share tends to \(1/4\), substitution in the exact primitive definitions yields
\[
A=\frac{200\sqrt5}{53\sqrt{203}},
\qquad b_1=\frac85,
\qquad b_2=\frac{43}{100},
\qquad \kappa=\frac{1393\sqrt5}{250\sqrt{203}}.
\]
Squaring positive radical endpoints and comparing integers verifies the displayed outward decimal enclosures and gives \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1<0\).

Both supports are bounded by \(1.15\), so their centered empirical fourth moments are eventually below \(2\).  Their variances and normalized-rank variances converge to positive constants exceeding \(1/100\), and all four shares converge to \(1/4\).  For deterministic quantiles of either bounded piecewise-constant density, uniform Riemann-sum approximation on each density piece gives
\[
N^{-3/2}K_N(u/\sqrt N)\longrightarrow u\int f^2
\]
uniformly for \(u\) in a fixed compact window; the finitely many density breakpoints contribute only \(O(N)\) pairs, which is \(o(N^{3/2})\).  Hence the pair-spacing, moment, share, and variance assumptions hold.  The singleton containing the displayed joint primitive vector is compact and is generated by this one array.  No interference, both complete randomizations, independent simple-random holdouts, and fixed thresholds hold by construction.

The split/assignment vector central limit theorem and the consistent selector studentizer proved in the transfer theorem give, uniformly in \(\rho\in I\),
\[
\Pr\{X_{n,s}>-113/100\}
\longrightarrow Q\{-113/100-A\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\}
\ge Q(-113/100).
\]
Independence across the two witness strata makes the both-selected probability's limit inferior at least \(Q(-113/100)^2\).  For the Fisher-completed candidate array, the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) local shifts do not affect limiting empirical second moments or ranks, while new candidate labels are null-centered.  The conditional finite-population vector theorem therefore makes each candidate selection probability converge in sampling probability to \(Q(-113/100)\), uniformly in \((\rho,h)\).  Candidate strata are independent, so their product converges to \(Q(-113/100)^2\).  Outward-rounded Gaussian evaluation gives
\[
Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534],
\]
which exceeds \(1/100\).  Thus the two-stratum array \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) satisfies every member condition of the now arbitrary-finite-stratum class and both cell-margin conditions.

For \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\), the two active cells have identical primitives, so their Gaussian conditional powers agree when their angles agree.  Both discrepancies are negative by \(\mathrm{prop{:}negative\mbox{-}mixture\mbox{-}primitives}\), and the weight-side theorem confines every endpoint maximizer to \(0<\theta<\theta_0\), where \(\theta_0=\arctan(b_2/b_1)\).

The numerical comparisons are interval statements, not floating-point equalities.  With \(100\)-bit Arb ball arithmetic, the null critical value at each queried box was enclosed to width \(2\cdot10^{-7}\) by opposite signs of its strictly decreasing defining equation.  The alternative integral was evaluated outwardly on \([c-ah,12]\), and the omitted tail is below \(Q(12)<10^{-31}\).  At the rational interior point this gives
\[
\Pi_j(5034/10000,25363/100000,33/20)
\in[0.8642862126664672633,0.8642862583791498921].
\]
For each endpoint, differentiation under the Gaussian integral and \(v^2\ge\rho_0\) give, on \(0\le\theta\le\theta_0\),
\[
|\partial_\theta\Pi_j|
\le
\frac{h}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,Q(c-ah)}
\left[b_2+
\frac{\gamma\sin\theta_0\{a+\gamma\sqrt{b_1^2+b_2^2}\}}
{1-\gamma^2}\right]=:L_\theta.
\]
A \(129\)-point rational mesh, with each interval evaluation enlarged by \(L_\theta\theta_0/256\), certifies
\[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(0.02,\theta,33/20)
\le0.8630457385441023483,
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(0.98,\theta,33/20)
\le0.8624116251942651582.
\]
The weight-side restriction covers angles outside the meshed interval.  Both endpoint upper bounds are strictly below the stated decimal bounds, whereas the interior lower endpoint is strictly above \(0.86428621266\).  The uniform transfer theorem identifies these Gaussian quantities with limiting rejection powers using the shifted sampling law and the separate zero-drift Fisher critical law.  Thus neither boundary holdout can maximize.  Continuity on compact \(I\) supplies a maximizer, so every maximizing holdout fraction is strictly interior.  This remains an explicit two-stratum subcase and does not restrict the ambient finite stratum set.

Fix a primitive vector on a stratum of \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\mbox{-}system}\), an active \(j=(C,s)\), and put
\[
p_j(\rho,\vartheta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\vartheta,\ell_s),
\qquad D_j=I\times[0,\pi/2].
\]
The residual-scale lemma gives \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\).  Define
\[
H_s(q,r)=\frac1{Q(c_s)}\int_{c_s}^{\infty}
\phi(z)Q\!\left(\frac{q-rz}{\sqrt{1-r^2}}\right)\,dz.
\]
On the compact correlation range, differentiation under the integral is dominated by a polynomial times a Gaussian density, and
\[
\partial_qH_s(q,r)=
-\frac1{Q(c_s)\sqrt{1-r^2}}
\int_{c_s}^{\infty}\phi(z)
\phi\!\left(\frac{q-rz}{\sqrt{1-r^2}}\right)\,dz<0.
\]
The same domination of local power series makes \(H_s\) real analytic.  The analytic implicit-function theorem makes its unique solution \(H_s(q,r)=\alpha\) analytic in \(r\), and a change of variable at the moving lower limit then proves that \(p_j\) is analytic on a neighborhood of \(D_j\).

Let \(Z_j=\{(\rho,\vartheta)\in D_j:\partial_\vartheta p_j=0\}\).  Its defining analytic function cannot vanish on a two-dimensional open set: analytic continuation would make \(p_j(\rho,\cdot)\) constant, contradicting the weight-side theorem in each of the three discrepancy signs.  Hence \(Z_j\) has dimension at most one.  The cited semianalytic-stratification lemma, applied compatibly with projection and the boundary, decomposes it into finitely many points and analytic arcs.  After finitely many cuts, every rank-one projected arc is an analytic graph \(\vartheta=\vartheta_{j\ell}(\rho)\), with Puiseux continuation at its recorded ramified endpoints; rank-zero arcs project to retained points.  Angular endpoint graphs are also included.

Fermat's rule and compactness of the angle interval now give, on each projected stratum,
\[
M_j(\rho)=\max_{\ell\in L_j}g_{j\ell}(\rho),
\qquad
g_{j\ell}(\rho)=p_j(\rho,\vartheta_{j\ell}(\rho)),
\]
for a finite branch set including angular endpoints.  Refine simultaneously over the finite set \(J\) by every nonidentical crossing, nontransverse crossing, candidate-value tie, and projected endpoint.  Identical branches and flat branches are retained symbolically.  The semianalytic lemma makes the refinement finite.  On each remaining open interval, branch order is fixed, so
\[
F(\rho)=\min_{j\in J}M_j(\rho)
\]
equals one analytic or Puiseux-continuable branch, with all ties retained.

An interior maximizer on a nonconstant active branch is a stationary root; a constant maximizing branch contributes its whole flat interval; every other maximizer is an endpoint or recorded transition.  Conversely, every retained candidate attaining \(V^\star\) is a global maximizer by definition.  This proves the necessary-and-sufficient holdout list.

For weights, cellwise maximization gives
\[
\max_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J}\min_{j\in J}p_j(\rho,\theta_j)
=\min_{j\in J}M_j(\rho)=F(\rho).
\]
The least-coordinate theorem transfers this identity to the original compact alternative set.  Therefore the full weight set at an optimal \(\rho\) is exactly
\[
\prod_{j=(C,s)\in J}
\{\theta_j\in[0,\pi/2]:\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge V^\star\}.
\]
Only finiteness of \(J\), inherited from fixed finite \(S\), was used.  The sign theorem restricts branches in positive, zero, negative, and mixed-sign regimes; the endpoint theorem and the two-stratum interior witness certify that both boundary and interior geometries actually occur.

By the branch theorem it suffices to certify the continuous function
\[
\Psi(\rho,\theta)=\min_{j=(C,s)\in J}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)
\]
on the compact finite-dimensional domain \(D=I\times[0,\pi/2]^J\).  A finite union of closed rational intervals presenting each coordinate projection of \(H\) gives \(\ell_s\) as its smallest left endpoint.

All Gaussian operations admit terminating rational enclosures.  On bounded intervals, the exponential power series with a Lagrange remainder encloses \(\phi\) and its derivatives.  For \(M>0\), integration by parts gives
\[
Q(M)\le\frac1M\int_M^\infty z\phi(z)\,dz=\frac{\phi(M)}M.
\]
Thus computably increasing truncation, bounded-interval quadrature with Taylor remainder, and symmetry give arbitrarily accurate outward enclosures of every integral and derivative in \(q_{\alpha,j}\) and \(\Pi_j\).

Because \(S\) is finite, compute a rational \(\underline q_c<\min_{s\in S}Q(c_s)\).  Choose rational \(M_q\) such that \(Q(M_q)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\underline q_c\).  For \(W=rZ+\sqrt{1-r^2}E\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\),
\[
\Pr(W>M_q\mid Z>c_s)<\alpha,
\qquad
\Pr(W>-M_q\mid Z>c_s)>\alpha.
\]
Hence all null critical values lie in \([-M_q,M_q]\).  On this compact interval and the compact correlation range, the absolute derivative
\[
\frac1{Q(c_s)\sqrt{1-r^2}}
\int_{c_s}^{\infty}\phi(z)
\phi\!\left(\frac{q-rz}{\sqrt{1-r^2}}\right)\,dz
\]
has an effective positive lower bound: restrict the integral to \([c_s,c_s+1]\), use \(v^2\ge\rho_0\), and take the minimum over finite \(S\).  Therefore monotone bisection terminates at any requested critical-value accuracy.

The alternative truncation thresholds lie in a computable compact interval, so their denominators have a positive computable lower bound.  Differentiating the power integrals, using the critical-value derivative bound, produces finite effective constants \(L_j\).  With \(L=\max_{j\in J}L_j\),
\[
|\Psi(x)-\Psi(y)|\le L\|x-y\|.
\]
Fix rational \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(0<\delta\le\varepsilon\).  A finite rational box subdivision of \(D\), fine enough for this modulus and evaluated by the preceding enclosures, yields bounds
\[
L_B\le\Psi(x)\le U_B\quad(x\in B),
\qquad U_B-L_B\le\delta.
\]
Set \(L^\star=\max_BL_B\) and \(U^\star=\max_BU_B\).  A box containing an optimizer and the preceding width bound give
\[
L^\star\le V^\star\le U^\star\le L^\star+\delta.
\]
Thus the value interval has width at most \(\varepsilon\).

Retain as the outer union boxes with \(U_B\ge L^\star\).  They contain every optimizer, and any point in one satisfies
\[
\Psi(x)\ge L_B\ge U_B-\delta\ge L^\star-\delta\ge V^\star-2\varepsilon.
\]
Retain as the inner union boxes with \(L_B\ge U^\star-\varepsilon\).  This union is nonempty because a box attaining \(L^\star\) qualifies, and every point in it satisfies \(\Psi(x)\ge V^\star-\varepsilon\).  Every comparison is between rational interval endpoints, so no exact-real equality oracle is used.

If the optional separation certificate is supplied, interval root-uniqueness tests isolate each winning root, complement exclusions remove all other roots, strict interval comparisons remove competing branch values, and a positive objective gap removes designs outside the winning boxes.  Applying the same tests to every factor of the product superlevel set excludes additional slack weights.  Only then is uniqueness asserted; otherwise the value interval and inner and outer optimizer-set boxes are the complete output.

Apply the conditioning-ratio lemma with \(\delta=\eta_n(B)\) and limiting cell lower bound \(m=m_n\).  Whenever \(m_n>\eta_n(B)\), it gives
\[
\sup_x|F_n(x\mid E_n)-F(x\mid E)|
\le\frac{2\eta_n(B)}{m_n-\eta_n(B)}.
\]
Thus \(\eta_n(B)=o(m_n)\) is sufficient.  If the limiting selected density is bounded below by \(g_n\) around its critical quantile, the quantile clause gives error at most
\[
\frac{2\eta_n(B)}{g_n\{m_n-\eta_n(B)\}},
\]
so any regime allowing density degeneration must also track \(g_n\).

No necessity statement follows from the declared remainder.  If \(\eta_n(B)\) is a valid decreasing upper sequence, then any decreasing \(\widetilde\eta_n(B)\ge\eta_n(B)\) tending to zero is also valid without changing a sampling law or a conditional error.  For example, after truncation at one, \(\widetilde\eta_n=\sqrt{\eta_n}\) is valid but may have a different ratio to \(m_n\).  Moreover, numerator and denominator approximation errors may cancel in their ratio, which an absolute upper bound cannot detect.

Finally, the sampling- and reference-selection assumptions impose the fixed positive constant \(\epsilon\) on every represented cell, eventually or with probability tending to one.  Hence no \(m_n\downarrow0\) regime lies in the frozen class, for any finite cardinality of \(S\).  A sharp failure frontier would require an enlarged class, a canonical minimal joint-approximation modulus, and explicit moving-threshold or boundary-density conditions.  The stated obstruction and universal sufficient relation are therefore the strongest consequences of the frozen primitives.

Put \(p_n=P_n(E_n)\), \(p=P(E)\), \(a_n(x)=P_n(A_n(x))\), and \(a(x)=P(A(x))\).  The assumptions give \(p_n\ge m-\delta>0\), and nesting gives \(0\le a(x)\le p\).  Therefore
\[
\left|\frac{a_n(x)}{p_n}-\frac{a(x)}p\right|
\le\frac{|a_n(x)-a(x)|}{p_n}
+\frac{a(x)|p_n-p|}{p_np}
\le\frac{2\delta}{m-\delta}.
\]
Taking the supremum proves the conditional-cdf inequality.  For quantiles, let \(q\) be the limiting \(p\)-quantile and let \(F_n,F\) be the conditional cdfs.  If \(0<t<a\), the density lower bound yields \(F(q-t)\le p-gt\) and \(F(q+t)\ge p+gt\).  When \(t>e/g\), uniform cdf error gives \(F_n(q-t)<p<F_n(q+t)\), so the generalized quantile \(q_n=\inf\{x:F_n(x)\ge p\}\) satisfies \(q-t<q_n\le q+t\).  Letting \(t\downarrow e/g\) proves \(|q_n-q|\le e/g\).

added_lemmas.statement: A finite family of real-analytic functions admits, locally, Weierstrass polynomial preparation and a compatible semianalytic stratification. A relatively compact semianalytic set consequently has finitely many connected components and a finite compatible stratification into connected real-analytic manifolds. Projections of relatively compact semianalytic sets are subanalytic, and the number of connected components of the fibers of a relatively compact subanalytic map is locally bounded. In dimension one, every punctured local semianalytic branch admits a real-analytic arc parametrization, with Puiseux preparation available as a proof mechanism. At a simple zero, the corresponding branch is an analytic graph by the analytic implicit-function theorem.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The random-holdout and stage--\(1\) complete-randomization assumptions give
\[
\mathsf P\{\mathcal A_{n,1}^{\mathrm{aug}}=a\}
=q_{n,1}^{\mathrm{aug}}(a)
\]
on the stated finite support, because the holdout and assignment are independent within each stratum and the strata are mutually independent. At \(h=0\), \(Y^{(0)}(1)=Y^{(0)}(0)=B\), so the sharp-null completion imputes every response needed to recompute the selector and rank statistic under every candidate action. prose_updates.tldr: For an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty stratum set \(S\) and two stages, each common holdout fraction \(\rho\) defines a chronological finite-population randomization law and a same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. Treating the randomized pair \((H,Z_1)\) as the first augmented action gives an exact Freidling--Zhao--Gao representation: recomputation on the full signed cell yields their computable conditional reference, while the finite-support tail argument gives exact selective level. A per-array common remainder transfers the shifted sampling law and the data-dependent zero-drift reference law, including random complement counts, studentization, rank stability, and quantiles. prose_updates.related_work: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's Propositions 1 and 2 are formally specialized by augmenting the first randomized action to \((H,Z_1)\): its known product law rerandomizes both the independent holdout and assignment, the selector is the complete label \(C\), and the stage-2 action depends on the past through that label. Sharp-zero imputability makes their reference computable, and the resulting restricted kernel is exactly the one enumerated here. Their broader multistage validity class supplies neither the Gaussian power limit nor the holdout--weight optimizer. Li and Ding supply the finite-population vector central limit theorem, while Shi and Ding supply quantitative permutation ingredients; the present transfer adds random complements, studentization, rank perturbations, signed-cell conditioning, and an imputed reference. Tian and Taylor provide a different independent-sampling selection-transfer architecture. Shenfeld and van Handel supply the Ehrhard--Borell theorem used to derive selected-quantile convexity. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu are a nonnested architectural comparator: their normal model-based policies optimize expected sample size subject to familywise-error and power constraints, not exact conditional-randomization local power, so no optimality result transfers. Chen and Andrews likewise study a parametric Gaussian adaptive experiment rather than this fixed-array design.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact test remains valid for any fixed finite number of prespecified strata because the randomized action law and complete signed cell factor into finite products. The optimization is cellwise in the weights but coupled through the common holdout and worst-cell minimum. A nonnegative discrepancy certificate permits the closed-form largest holdout; a negative discrepancy can instead make an interior holdout strictly better, as the explicit two-stratum subcase proves. prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The transfer is per admissible baseline array: one deterministic remainder is uniform over its holdouts, weights, compact alternatives, and finitely many active cells, but no rate is uniform across the qualitative population class. Selection probabilities are bounded below by a fixed margin, so the result does not cover shrinking cells. The reference approximation is in the sampling probability associated with each design value, not under a simultaneous coupling of all holdouts. The two-stratum mixture is only an interior-optimum witness inside the arbitrary finite-stratum theory. The augmented-action proposition specializes Freidling--Zhao--Gao validity and computability only; all Gaussian and optimization conclusions require the separate finite-population transfer proved here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Finite-sample exactness is limited to the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero null. Positive alternatives are local constant effects on fixed potential-outcome arrays, and every design value has its own sampling law, dataset, completion, and reference kernel. The ambient stratum set is arbitrary but fixed, finite, and nonempty; the stage count remains two, the holdout fraction is common across strata, and \(J\) is finite. The scalar power formula applies only after complete signed-cell factor cancellation. The explicit negative mixture remains a two-stratum witness and does not establish uniqueness of its interior optimizer. General computation returns tolerance-certified value and optimizer-set boxes; a unique design is reported only with an explicit separation certificate. Binary outcomes, nonzero sharp-null inversion, weak average-effect nulls, shrinking selection margins, outcome-dependent deterministic splits, and continuous-biomarker cutoffs remain outside scope.
